title: Team cadence symphony — Q3 exec update & all-staff slate (draft)
body:
Purpose
This doc is a working draft for the Q3 executive update and the corresponding all-staff segment. Goal is to provide a concise narrative (3-minute exec update + 12-minute all-hands segment) that connects: strategy -> priorities -> measurable signals (OKRs) -> asks for teams.

Context and framing
- Company thesis reminder (one line): Shift from model ownership to serving economics — we win by predictable, affordable inference at scale.
- Q2 summary (one-liner): Hosted growth steady; Dedicated sales pipeline ahead of plan; a short-term reliability incident in May highlighted a route-fallback gap we fixed.
- Tone for Q3: pragmatic momentum. Emphasize measurable throughput improvements, new Private deployments pilot, and lowering hosted unit cost.

Proposed all-staff run (12 minutes)
1) Opening (1 minute) — CEO / co-founder: 30s recap of why we exist; 30s signal of confidence (metrics headline).
2) Headline numbers (2 minutes) — COO / Head of Revenue: top-level signals (ARR velocity, Dedicated commit pipeline, unit cost delta). Slide: 3 metrics with sparkline.
3) Engineering highlight (3 minutes) — VP Eng: short demo video (15s) + what it means: 1) 18% median token latency improvement on common seq lengths; 2) 12% cost-per-token improvement via batching and kernel tuning.
4) Product/Customer story (2 minutes) — Solutions Eng or CS: customer vignette of migrating to Dedicated with SLA and reduced variance; one quote.
5) Ask & commitments (2 minutes) — Exec: 3 company asks for the next quarter (see below).
6) Quick Q&A / Slack-driven (2 minutes) — capture top 3 questions, triage deeper answers to follow.

Draft headline metrics to show
- Hosted API: 2.1M monthly active requests (+16% q/q) — show percent from streaming features.
- Dedicated revenue pipeline: $1.8M TCV in committed prospects (motion: expedite onboarding flows).
- Private pilot: 3 customers in pilot, target 8 by end-Q3.
- Platform economics: median token cost (hosted) down 12% vs Q2 baseline.
- Reliability SLO compliance: 99.92% (improving to 99.97 goal).

Draft Q3 OKR slate (high level, 3 company OKRs + supporting signals)
- OKR 1: Make inference predictable at scale
  - KR1.1: Achieve <80ms median token latency on hosted p50 for seq len <=512
  - KR1.2: 99.97% availability for hosted inference endpoints (global)
  - KR1.3: 3x reduction in high-latency tail incidents (p99 -> p99.9 improvements)
- OKR 2: Improve unit economics so customers can scale affordably
  - KR2.1: 15% reduction in cost-per-effective-token across top 10 workloads
  - KR2.2: Automated batching & cache adoption enabled for 60% of traffic
  - KR2.3: Ship first quantization profiles for two popular model families in catalog
- OKR 3: Expand enterprise-ready private deployments and adoption
  - KR3.1: 8 private deployment pilots executed and at least 3 converted to license agreements
  - KR3.2: Add KMS/HSM integration for one major cloud provider and one on-prem flow
  - KR3.3: Launch a self-serve installer prototype for demo installs (internal use)

Top company asks (what we need from teams)
1) Platform teams: prioritize autoscaling stability improvements and rollout a default autoscaler policy by mid-Q3.
2) Product + DevRel: produce three vertical-focused quickstarts for Dedicated (SaaS, FinServ, Health) so PMs can demo value to prospects.
3) Sales + Solutions Eng: shorten Dedicated onboarding checklist to reduce TTD (time to demo) from 14d -> 7d.

Risks and mitigations (short list)
- Risk: Batching improvements hurt latency-sensitive tail. Mitigation: Canary gating + per-route overrides.
- Risk: Private installs take longer than expected (network + security hoops). Mitigation: standardize an audit-ready checklist + partner with one channel integrator.
- Risk: Feature fragmentation (different behavior across hosted/dedicated/private). Mitigation: add demo matrix to product docs + invest in conformance tests.

Communication artifacts to produce (owner and timing)
- One-pager for sales (Marcus P.) — deadline: 2026-03-20 — content: Dedicated quickstart bullets + value metrics.
- Engineering FAQ (Avery C. + Leah O.) — deadline: 2026-03-22 — content: what changed, rollback knobs, expected infra impact.
- All-staff slide deck (Sofia R.) — deadline: 2026-03-25 — 6 slides: narrative, 3 metrics, customer vignette, asks, Q&A slide.

Open questions / items for exec sync (to resolve before deck finalization)
- Which single customer story do we lead with? Options: Retail pilot A (cost savings), FinServ pilot B (SLA + compliance), or Marketplace C (throughput). Recommend: FinServ B for credibility on Private.
- Do we lock the headline latency target to p50 or p75 for the narrative? Exec preference: p50 is marketable, but p75 may be more representative.
- Should the CEO put a strategic bet statement (one line) about partnerships and channel plays this quarter? Draft line proposed: "This quarter we prove that predictable inference is not just faster — it’s repeatable, auditable, and economical for regulated customers."

Notes-to-self (draft tone and cadence)
- Keep slides visually minimal: numbers + one supporting visual per slide. No more than 6 bullets total.
- Avoid deep engineering jargon in the 12-minute segment. Reserve technical deep dives to follow-up office hours.
- Collect 2–3 customer quotes (short) by 2026-03-18. Leah to coordinate.

Meeting prep checklist (for final rehearsal)
- Slide deck ready and uploaded to drive (owner: Sofia)
- Rehearsal with CEO + VP Eng + Head of Revenue (30m) scheduled 2026-03-27
- Slack thread for live Q&A moderation created (owner: Jonah B.)

Appendix (links and references)
- Q2 incidents postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/Q2-INCIDENTS-POSTMORTEM
- Hosted performance dashboards (internal): dash://perf/hosted/q2-summary
- Dedicated sales pipeline board: JIRA-PIPELINE-BOARD

-- end of draft --

(Comments welcome — this is intentionally concise; will expand the deck notes and speaker script after exec sync.)
